summary: Reviewed the World Cup SEO optimisation spec against the supplied current page implementation and project conventions. The spec has a sensible intent shift toward fixtures-first search demand, but several proposed copy and structured-data changes depend on unverified operational, tournament, or repository facts that the pack does not substantiate. The highest-risk assumptions are customer-facing claims that CLAUDE.md says must come from the SSOT before being published.
appears_sound: Keeping the URL and ISR unchanged is well supported: the current page already uses `/live-sport/world-cup` and `revalidate = 60 * 60 * 24` in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx`.

The spec correctly identifies duplicate content: the current page has both three info cards and a `Matchday Essentials` feature grid repeating screens, sound, kitchen, and parking claims in `app/live-sport/world-cup/page.tsx`.
The Event schema performer concern is valid: the current implementation sets `performer` to FIFA even though the venue event is The Anchor screening matches, not FIFA performing at the pub.

findings.description: The spec proposes multiple customer-facing factual claims without proving they were checked against `docs/SSOT.md`, which CLAUDE.md makes mandatory before page copy, JSON-LD, meta descriptions, or alt text. This affects hours, parking capacity, free-to-air broadcast claims, extended hours, and England group details.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md says to read `docs/SSOT.md` before any customer-facing content and not invent facts, while the spec includes unverified claims such as BBC/ITV coverage, Group L opponents, Fri-Sat hours, and midnight extensions.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The spec notes one hours item should be verified against SSOT, so the author may have intended this as a pre-implementation checkpoint rather than a final instruction.
findings.what_would_confirm: Check every proposed operational and tournament claim against `docs/SSOT.md`, `SSOT.json`, and a current authoritative fixture source before implementation.

findings.description: The spec tells implementers to add a free-parking claim with placeholder text `up to [X] cars`, which cannot ship in customer-facing copy. Leaving this unresolved risks either a literal placeholder on the page or an invented parking number.
findings.evidence: The local area rewrite says `Free parking for up to [X] cars`, while the current page uses `PARKING.capacity` from constants in several places.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The placeholder may be intended to remind the implementer to use `PARKING.capacity`.
findings.what_would_confirm: Replace `[X]` in the spec with the existing `PARKING.capacity` pattern or a SSOT-backed numeric value before coding.

findings.description: The spec adds `All matches on BBC and ITV (free to air)` as a first bullet, but that can imply The Anchor will show all World Cup matches, contradicting the page rule that only matches during opening hours or early-opening windows are shown. This would create a material mismatch between user expectation and the fixtures table.
findings.evidence: The current page says matches outside opening hours are not shown, while the spec's proposed bullet says `All matches on BBC and ITV (free to air)` under `What We're Showing`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The intended meaning may be that UK broadcast rights are free-to-air, not that the pub screens every match.
findings.what_would_confirm: Rewrite the bullet to distinguish broadcast availability from venue screening availability, for example that matches The Anchor shows are BBC/ITV free-to-air broadcasts.

findings.description: The proposed FAQ says all World Cup 2026 matches are broadcast free to air on BBC and ITV in the UK, but the pack contains no authoritative source for 2026 rights or coverage scope. Because this is customer-facing and time-sensitive, it should not be published from assumption.
findings.evidence: The FAQ addition states `All World Cup 2026 matches are broadcast free to air on BBC and ITV in the UK`, but the pack only contains the spec and current page, not an external rights source or SSOT confirmation.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: BBC and ITV have historically carried FIFA World Cup coverage in the UK, so the claim may be true.
findings.what_would_confirm: Verify current UK broadcast rights from an authoritative source and, if it is an operational marketing fact, add or cite it through the SSOT process.

findings.description: The proposed England Group L line names Croatia, Ghana, and Panama, but the pack provides no fixture data or authoritative tournament draw source. If wrong or changed, this would be a highly visible factual error on an SEO landing page.
findings.evidence: The spec says `England are in Group L alongside Croatia, Ghana and Panama`, while the included current page only derives England fixtures dynamically from match placeholders.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The statement may come from research outside the pack that was not included.
findings.what_would_confirm: Verify the 2026 draw and England group from a current authoritative source before hardcoding the sentence, or derive group context from trusted fixture data.

findings.description: The keyword strategy is internally contradictory: it lists `football pub near me` and `pub showing football near me` as primary targets, then says not to target `football pub near me` because the parent `/live-sport` page owns it. That ambiguity can lead to cannibalisation between the World Cup page and parent live-sport page.
findings.evidence: The spec's primary targets table includes `football pub near me` and `pub showing football near me`, but the `DO NOT target` list says `football pub near me` belongs to `/live-sport`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The author may intend light semantic inclusion but not primary optimisation for the World Cup page.
findings.what_would_confirm: Revise the keyword section to identify which terms are primary for this page versus only contextual internal-link or local relevance terms.

findings.description: The spec assumes a `BreadcrumbJsonLd` component exists on the parent page and can be reused here, but the pack contains no parent page implementation or component import path. This is a codebase-fit risk because the implementer could invent a new schema pattern instead of using the existing one.
findings.evidence: The schema section says `The <BreadcrumbJsonLd> component exists on the parent /live-sport page`, but the Review Pack includes only the current World Cup page snippet and no parent page source.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The component may exist exactly as described outside the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Inspect the parent `/live-sport` page and reuse its Breadcrumb JSON-LD component and import path if present.

findings.description: The internal-linking tasks require edits to `/live-sport`, the homepage, and blog posts, but none of those files are in the pack. As written, the spec overstates the evidence for zero parent links and possible homepage CTAs, so these should remain verification tasks rather than implementation facts.
findings.evidence: The spec claims the parent page has zero links to `/live-sport/world-cup` and asks to verify homepage and blog links, while the pack has no related file contents for those pages or posts.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The user concerns may have come from a separate audit not included in this pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Search the parent page, homepage, sitemap, and content/blog sources for existing `/live-sport/world-cup` links before adding new links.

findings.description: The spec says the FAQPage schema will automatically pick up new FAQ items via `FAQAccordionWithSchema`, but the current page also emits a separate JSON-LD script containing only Event schema. If Breadcrumb JSON-LD is added as another script or array without checking existing schema composition, duplicate or fragmented structured data could be introduced.
findings.evidence: The current page renders `jsonLdSafeStringify([eventSchema])` and separately renders `FAQAccordionWithSchema`, while the spec proposes adding BreadcrumbList JSON-LD without defining the composition pattern.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: Multiple JSON-LD scripts are valid, and the existing component may intentionally manage FAQ schema separately.
findings.what_would_confirm: Confirm the repo's structured-data pattern and validate the final page in a schema validator after adding Event, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage.

findings.description: The spec says to remove the intro copy section but also says `World Cup Pub Near Heathrow` stays in the H1, without specifying where that H1 should live after the intro section is removed. This can accidentally remove the page's primary commercial heading or create an H1/H2 hierarchy mismatch.
findings.evidence: The section-order change removes `Intro copy + H1`, while the metadata rationale says `World Cup Pub Near Heathrow` stays in the H1.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The intent may be to keep the existing `PageTitle` text but move it into the fixtures-first section.
findings.what_would_confirm: Clarify the final heading hierarchy, including the exact H1 text and placement after the hero.

empty_categories: No direct security or data-access risks found in the proposed spec, since the changes are content, metadata, internal links, and JSON-LD only.
No database or RLS assumptions found; CLAUDE.md says this website has no database and the spec does not add one.
No obvious performance-scale issue found; keeping 24h ISR and the existing resilient fixture fetch avoids adding runtime pressure.
